title: AutoSkewBMT: Autonomously Synthesizing Optimized Integrity Authentication Mechanism for DNN Accelerators
problem: DNN accelerators require memory security (encryption and integrity authentication) to protect data, but standard approaches like Bonsai Merkle Tree (BMT) integrity checks incur prohibitive overhead in high-throughput accelerator workloads, creating a bottleneck between security and performance.
motivation: Domain-specific DNN accelerators face surging data security demands, but memory authentication overhead directly degrades throughput; standard BMT configurations are not workload-optimized, leaving performance on the table.
method: The system automatically customizes tree structures for integrity checking by reshaping the Bonsai Merkle Tree—a hierarchical format where each level holds cryptographic fingerprints to detect data tampering—to match how the specific DNN workload accesses memory. It runs an algorithm to explore different tree shapes and selects whichever one verifies memory fastest while maintaining the cryptographic guarantee that nothing has been changed. By matching the tree shape to actual memory access patterns, it eliminates the normal tradeoff between speed and security.
key_novelty: Automatically reshaping the integrity-checking tree to match each workload's memory access patterns eliminates the speed-versus-security bottleneck in DNN accelerator data verification.
contributions: Novel design space generation algorithm for BMT skewing
Autonomous synthesis framework (AutoSkewBMT) for integrity systems
32% improvement over state-of-the-art on general DNN workloads

metrics.other: throughput overhead reduction via workload-matched tree structure

baselines: prior memory authentication schemes for accelerators
limitations: Limited to Merkle-tree-based authentication; applicability to other integrity schemes (HMAC, signatures) not discussed.
primary_theme: workload-aware integrity authentication for memory-constrained DNN accelerators
